words.gloss: adhering to the side of justice

literal: Impartiality called one thing is indeed good, if, towards all classes of people, adhering to the side of justice, to conduct oneself is achieved.
translation: The single virtue called impartiality is indeed excellent, if one can conduct oneself with equal fairness towards all classes of people.
modern: நண்பர், பகைவர், அயலார் ஆகிய அனைத்துப் பிரிவினரிடமும் நடுவுநிலைமையோடு நடந்து கொள்ளப் பெற்றால், தகுதி என்று சொல்லப்படும் அந்த ஒரு பண்பு மட்டுமே ஒருவருக்குப் பெரும் நன்மையாகும்.
explanation: This couplet introduces the chapter on impartiality by defining its supreme value. The word 'தகுதி' (fitness/equity) is used here to mean impartiality or fairness. The poet states that this single quality is a great virtue, provided one can practice it consistently across different 'பகுதி' (divisions or categories of people, such as friends, enemies, and strangers). The phrase 'பாற்பட்டு ஒழுகப் பெறின்' emphasizes that true impartiality lies in actively adhering to the side of justice in all one's actions.
